attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts the financial comparisons and free-user economics.

semantics.note: The normalization captures the asserted current comparisons. The contract retains the numerical details underlying the free-user comparison.

contract.note: Comparable financial definitions and matching annualized advertising and serving costs are fair requirements. The latest completed quarter is a reasonable reference period; missing comparable records prevent resolution regardless.

evidence.note: A dated company disclosure of total advertising run rate. It neither isolates free-user revenue and costs nor establishes a continuing revenue ceiling.
Timely reporting identifies incompatible revenue recognition and reporting intervals. Unreconciled headline figures cannot establish or reverse the claimed comparisons.

reviews.rationale: The packet lacks comparable revenue, growth and expense records for both companies and a matching free-user serving-cost allocation. The advertising disclosure and revenue-recognition caveat do not settle any complete comparison.

attribution.note: The annual cost-growth guarantee is Zitron's own assertion, following quoted company disclosures.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves substantial growth every year. The guarantee is firm, with no hedge or stated end date.

contract.note: Company-wide annual operating costs are an ordinary reading. The chosen cost measure and meaning of substantial growth affect eventual grading, but a flat or declining comparable year fairly defeats the guarantee.

evidence.note: The secondary summary supplies historical expenses and management expectations about quarterly fluctuations. Neither establishes a future annual cost outcome.

reviews.rationale: No complete post-publication annual comparison exists in the packet. Historical growth cannot establish an unlimited annual guarantee, and no flat or declining future year meets the early-resolution rule.

attribution.note: Zitron directly endorses the prediction of intensifying industry pressures.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm worsening prediction. The reference to desperation describes the predicted trajectory rather than a separately specified antecedent.

contract.note: Broad intensification of the named pressures is a fair ordinary reading. Aggregation and persistence requirements are evaluator interpretations, so isolated developments cannot determine the result.

evidence.note: Reports lending pressure, including developments preceding publication and an alternative loan facility. It does not establish sustained post-publication deterioration across the indicators.
Reports prospective IPO pressure alongside continuing investor interest. Negotiations and sentiment establish neither a completed valuation nor a sustained broad trend.
The initial funding closing shows continued access to capital alongside reduced ambitions. This isolated transaction establishes neither broad worsening nor sustained easing.

reviews.rationale: The short observation window contains financing pressure and continued investment, but no sustained comparison across all named indicators. Further Grok restrictions are unverified, and no event satisfies the contract's early-resolution rule.

attribution.note: The exhaustion inference is Zitron's own, drawn from reporting he endorses about fundraising and investor targeting.

semantics.note: The normalization captures his asserted present exhaustion of institutional willingness and its connection to seeking other investors.

contract.note: Testing additional willingness beyond existing commitments on contemporaneous terms fairly captures the assertion. Initial participation alone cannot contradict it.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous reporting establishes institutional participation, reduced allocations and an unfinished round. It does not identify willingness to invest beyond existing commitments.

reviews.rationale: An open round and institutional participation do not establish remaining willingness, while a reduced fundraising target does not prove exhaustion across the three investor groups. The packet lacks the additional commitments or investor communications needed to decide.
